subject: geog
source: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460) syllabus for examination in 2027, 2028 and 2029 — Cambridge International; Year 10 covers Paper 1 physical geography (topics 1–5) and geographical skills

weeks.topic: Geographical skills: map reading, grid references and scale
objectives: Give four- and six-figure grid references
Measure distances using scale on 1:25 000 and 1:50 000 maps
Use compass directions

weeks.topic: Map skills: contours, gradient and cross-sections
objectives: Interpret relief from contours and spot heights
Calculate gradient
Draw and annotate cross-sections

weeks.topic: Drainage basins and the hydrological cycle
objectives: Describe inputs, stores, flows and outputs of a drainage basin
Explain the role of rivers in the water cycle

weeks.topic: River processes: erosion, transport and deposition; the Bradshaw model
objectives: Describe hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution
Describe transport processes
Apply the Bradshaw model downstream

weeks.topic: River landforms of the upper course: V-shaped valleys, waterfalls and gorges
objectives: Explain the formation of waterfalls and gorges
Describe interlocking spurs and potholes

weeks.topic: River landforms of the middle and lower course: meanders, ox-bow lakes, levees and deltas
objectives: Explain the formation of meanders and ox-bow lakes
Describe floodplains, levees and deltas

weeks.topic: Flood hydrographs and the causes of river flooding
objectives: Draw and interpret flood hydrographs
Explain physical and human causes of floods

weeks.topic: Opportunities of rivers and a river flood (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain opportunities such as water supply, farming, transport and energy
Describe causes and impacts of a specific river flood

weeks.topic: Managing rivers: flood defences and river pollution (detailed specific example)
objectives: Compare hard and soft flood management
Describe causes, effects and management of a specific river pollution example

weeks.topic: Coastal processes: wave types, erosion, transport and longshore drift
objectives: Compare constructive and destructive waves
Describe coastal erosion and longshore drift

weeks.topic: Coastal erosion landforms on concordant and discordant coastlines
objectives: Explain headlands and bays on discordant coasts
Explain the cliff–cave–arch–stack–stump sequence

weeks.topic: Coastal deposition landforms: beaches, spits, bars and tombolos
objectives: Explain the formation of beaches, spits and bars
Describe sand dunes and salt marshes

weeks.topic: Coral reefs and mangroves: conditions, value and threats
objectives: Describe conditions for coral reef and mangrove growth
Explain their value and threats to them

weeks.topic: Tropical storms: formation, impacts and responses
objectives: Explain the conditions needed for tropical storms
Describe their structure and impacts on coasts

weeks.topic: Review: map skills, rivers and coasts
objectives: Practise map and hydrograph questions
Revise river and coastal landform diagrams

weeks.topic: Coastal management: hard and soft engineering (detailed specific examples)
objectives: Compare sea walls, groynes, beach nourishment and managed retreat
Evaluate a coastal management scheme

weeks.topic: The Antarctic ecosystem: characteristics and adaptations
objectives: Describe the climate, food web and biodiversity of Antarctica
Explain adaptations of plants and animals

weeks.topic: Threats to the Antarctic ecosystem and their management
objectives: Explain threats from tourism, fishing, mineral exploitation and climate change
Evaluate the Antarctic Treaty and conservation measures

weeks.topic: The tropical rainforest ecosystem: structure, climate and nutrient cycle
objectives: Describe the climate and layers of the rainforest
Explain the nutrient cycle and biodiversity

weeks.topic: Threats to tropical rainforests: deforestation in the Amazon
objectives: Explain causes of deforestation such as cattle ranching, logging and mining
Describe local and global impacts

weeks.topic: Managing tropical rainforests sustainably (detailed specific example)
objectives: Evaluate protected areas, ecotourism and sustainable forestry
Assess a specific management example

weeks.topic: Earth's structure and plate boundaries
objectives: Describe the layers of the Earth
Explain convergent, divergent and conservative plate boundaries
Describe the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes

weeks.topic: Processes and features of earthquakes and volcanoes
objectives: Describe focus, epicentre and seismic waves
Compare composite and shield volcanoes

weeks.topic: Impacts of tectonic hazards and magnitude scales
objectives: Describe primary and secondary impacts
Use the moment magnitude scale and VEI

weeks.topic: Managing tectonic hazards: an earthquake (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain prediction, protection and preparation
Evaluate responses to a specific earthquake

weeks.topic: Managing tectonic hazards: a volcanic eruption (detailed specific example)
objectives: Explain why people live near volcanoes
Evaluate monitoring and responses to a specific eruption

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: rivers, coasts, ecosystems and tectonic hazards
objectives: Complete timed Paper 1 style questions
Use detailed specific examples in extended answers

weeks.topic: Natural causes of climate change
objectives: Explain variations in solar output, orbital changes and volcanic eruptions
Use evidence of past climate change

weeks.topic: Human causes of climate change: the enhanced greenhouse effect
objectives: Explain the greenhouse effect and enhanced greenhouse effect
Identify sources of greenhouse gases

weeks.topic: Impacts of climate change at local, national and global scales
objectives: Describe sea-level rise, extreme weather and ecosystem change
Explain impacts on people in HICs, MICs and LICs

weeks.topic: Responses to climate change: mitigation and adaptation (detailed specific example)
objectives: Compare mitigation and adaptation strategies
Evaluate international agreements and a specific response

weeks.topic: Graphical skills: climate graphs, scatter graphs and systems diagrams
objectives: Construct and interpret climate graphs
Draw scatter graphs with lines of best fit
Interpret systems diagrams

weeks.topic: GIS, photographs and satellite images
objectives: Interpret photographs and satellite images
Use GIS to identify patterns and trends
Detect bias in written sources

weeks.topic: Fieldwork skills: the route to geographical enquiry
objectives: Describe the stages of an enquiry
Choose equipment such as flow meters, clinometers and quadrats
Carry out a risk assessment

weeks.topic: Mathematical skills: statistics, indices and drawing conclusions
objectives: Calculate mean, median, mode and range
Use indices and significant figures
Draw conclusions from data

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: physical geography and skills
objectives: Complete a full Paper 1 style exam
Apply skills to unfamiliar maps and data

weeks.topic: Review: climate change, ecosystems and fieldwork skills
objectives: Correct errors from end-of-year exams
Build detailed specific example revision cards
